clue.text: Don't admit Jones's partner's holding is a 5

indicators.note: holding means the first piece wraps round the following pieces

parts.note: Dow is partnered with Jones in the Dow Jones stock index
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to confess what Mr Jones's associate is keeping.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a cross-reference to another entry, but it is simply the number, written in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown or repudiate something is to refuse to acknowledge it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Don't talk during homework, gorgeous!

indicators.note: during means one piece sits in the middle of the other

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is work done on your own home
sh is the hushing sound telling someone to be quiet

explanation.surface: A parent hushes a child doing homework while calling them gorgeous.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal British word for very good-looking, said of an attractive person.

clue.text: Cryptic clues with a religious origin, unlike this

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or encoded, so the letters of the word clues are disguised by rearranging
origin points to the first letter, where the word religious begins

explanation.surface: A remark that crosswords began in church, said of a puzzle which is not so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points back to 'religious', so the definition reads 'not religious'; 'Cryptic' looks like it describes the clues but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Worldly, non-religious matters are the opposite of the religious origin the clue mentions.

clue.text: See 22
We keep signs in place outside their opening time: we are teasingly famous for …

indicators.note: keep means the word We holds everything else between its two letters

parts.note: omens are signs or portents

indicators.note: outside means the Latin phrase wraps round the next piece

parts.note: in situ is Latin for in its original place

indicators.note: opening picks the initial letter of the word their

explanation.surface: Members put up notices where they meet, and are gently mocked for something that continues in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: IN SITU goes round T (start of 'their') to make INSTITU, then T for 'time' follows. The definition runs on into 5-down: the WI (a British countrywomen's club) is joked about for jam-making and singing Blake's hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Women's Institute is a British countrywomen's organisation, long teased for being all jam-making and hymn-singing.

clue.text: It takes a god to injure (badly) hell

annotationWithheld.why: It takes a god to injure (badly) hell: the parse is PIT inside an anagram of JURE, with the 'in' of 'injure' as the insertion indicator, so one word is both indicator and fodder, which the grammar cannot split
annotationWithheld.clue: It takes a god to injure (badly) hell

clue.text: … a chap with record player not quietly reading with small boy around

indicators.note: around means the boy's name wraps all the other pieces

parts.note: Jem is a short form of the boy's name Jeremy
a man is a chap
a DJ, disc jockey, plays records

indicators.note: not quietly means the musical sign for quiet, p for piano, is dropped

parts.note: perusal is the act of reading something closely

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: a fellow with a disc jockey, reading loudly with a lad round about.
explanation.walkthrough: PERUSAL loses its P (piano, quiet in music) to give ERUSAL. The definition is the end of 4-down: what the Women's Institute is teased for, jam-making and singing the hymn 'Jerusalem'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jam-making and singing Blake's 'Jerusalem' are the activities the Women's Institute is jokingly said to live for.

clue.text: Far from centre page, goddess in danger

indicators.note: in means the first pair of pieces is placed inside the word for danger

parts.note: peril means danger
Hera is the Greek queen of the gods

explanation.surface: A goddess on a centre page spread finds herself in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Peripheral things lie at the edge, away from the middle; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Hint by old actor in Essex

parts.note: a tip is a hint
Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated Victorian and Edwardian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A tip-off from a veteran performer who lives in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a place: Tiptree is a village in Essex, a county east of London, famous for its jam factory, which fits the puzzle's jam theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptree is a village located in the county of Essex, so the clue defines it by where it lies.

clue.text: First notes after second notes in church?

indicators.note: after places the following piece behind the earlier one in the answer

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale, so two of them are second notes
doh or do is the first note of the sol-fa scale, so dos are first notes

explanation.surface: A question about the order of hymn notes sung in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' reverses the clue's order, so the first notes go at the end. The question mark admits the definition is only a location: a reredos is a screen behind a church altar.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen behind a church altar, so it is a thing found in church.

clue.text: Finding commerce so sadly devoid of ecstasy, I ferry the kids

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged
devoid of means one letter is taken out of the words before

parts.note: E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A suburban parent complains that trade has lost its thrill while driving children about.
explanation.walkthrough: One E of the two in COMMERCE SO goes, leaving COMMRCESO to rearrange; the blog notes 'devoid of' might seem to ask for both to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A soccer mom is an American type of suburban mother who drives her children to their sports and activities.

clue.text: Last words on monarch are not so green

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the final inscription on a grave
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: The epitaph on a dead king shows he was less naive than thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is riper is less green or unripe, the comparative of mature.

clue.text: University on its last drink

indicators.note: its last picks the final letter of the word University

parts.note: ale is a drink

explanation.surface: Students at a college who are down to the final round.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the Y before the ALE. The whole clue doubles as the definition: an American university, its final letter sitting on a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale is one of the American Ivy League universities in Connecticut.

clue.text: Loveless marriages — good, dangerous, or boring?

indicators.note: loveless means the letter that looks like zero, love in tennis, is dropped

parts.note: unions are marriages
pi, short for pious, means good
red is the colour that signals danger

explanation.surface: A question whether marriages without love are good, risky or just dull.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O (zero in tennis); taking it out of UNIONS gives UNINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uninspired is dull and lacking imagination, which is what boring means.

clue.text: Angel about to go to hell — or limbo?

indicators.note: about means the word for angel goes round the other piece

parts.note: an angel is a financial backer, of a show for instance
to burn is to suffer in hell's fires

explanation.surface: A heavenly being is about to be sent down to the underworld, or stuck between.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angel' and 'hell' look heavenly and infernal, but an angel here is a theatre investor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the back burner is shelved and left pending, much as in limbo.

clue.text: Top man serving drinks first to man of fashion

indicators.note: top means take the top off, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: a barman serves drinks
I is the Roman numeral one, so first

explanation.surface: A head waiter serves cocktails first to a fashionable gent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top man' looks like a phrase for a boss, but 'Top' is a verb: behead.
explanation.definitionFit: Giorgio Armani is a famous Italian fashion designer, so he is a man of fashion.

clue.text: Do we drive vehicles off the road? Golly!

definitions.text: Do we drive vehicles off the road?
definitions.meaning: a playful reading: people who drive jeeps could be called this
an exclamation of surprise, like gosh or crikey

explanation.definitionFit: Jeepers is a mild exclamation of surprise, and jokingly also people driving jeeps.

clue.text: Bush beat me for king and I get snatched by French composer

indicators.note: get snatched by means the pieces are taken inside the composer's name

parts.note: Paul Dukas was the French composer of The Sorcerer's Apprentice
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A loser explains that a king and he were captured by a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Dukakis was the Democratic candidate whom George H W Bush beat in the 1988 US presidential election.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Dukakis lost the 1988 presidential race to George Bush, so he can say Bush beat him.

clue.text: Sideboard behind the scenes?

definitions.meaning: a piece of furniture with shelves and cupboards for dishes
in a theatre, the person who helps actors with their costumes backstage

explanation.definitionFit: A dresser is both a kitchen sideboard and a theatre assistant who dresses actors backstage.

clue.text: Gear numbers show state of anxiety

parts.note: kit is gear or equipment
tens are numbers

explanation.surface: Equipment with numbered settings reveals how nervous someone is.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'have kittens' is British slang for being very anxious or upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Having kittens is an idiom for being extremely nervous or agitated.

clue.text: Get together again? No kidding

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to form an alliance once more
an exclamation meaning honestly or is that so

explanation.definitionFit: Really means truly, as in no kidding, and read as re-ally means join forces again.

clue.text: Happy girl? It turns up twice in field

indicators.note: in means the repeated piece is placed inside the word for field

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field

indicators.note: twice means the reversed word appears two times
turns up means the word It is read backwards in this down clue

explanation.surface: A cheerful girl keeps popping up in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: IT reversed is TI, twice gives TITI, placed in LEA. The name comes from Latin laetitia, joy, hence 'Happy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Letitia is a girl's name derived from the Latin for gladness or joy.

clue.text: Zeal displayed by English humanists

indicators.note: displayed suggests the letters of humanists are laid out in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Ardour shown by English scholars of the humanities.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeal and enthusiasm both mean eager, energetic devotion to something.

clue.text: In rock, pull a passenger out of line

indicators.note: In means the following pieces are placed inside the word for rock

parts.note: to sway is to rock to and fro
to tow is to pull

explanation.surface: Someone at sea, swaying, hauls a misbehaving traveller out of the queue.
explanation.definitionFit: A stowaway travels hidden without paying, a passenger who has broken the rules.

clue.text: Outlook when king and lord briefly struggle amid great success

indicators.note: amid means the other pieces sit in the middle of the word for success

parts.note: a wow is a great hit or success
R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king
Ld is the short form of Lord
to vie is to struggle or compete

explanation.surface: A view of how king and nobleman fight in the midst of triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: A world view is one's overall outlook on life, a direct synonym.

clue.text: See 21
Brilliance of man confined by some of his elders

indicators.note: confined by means the word for man is enclosed in the other piece
some of means only part of the word is kept, the end being cut off

parts.note: his elders are his seniors
he stands for a man

explanation.surface: The glitter of a man hemmed in by older relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of' marks a trimmed synonym: only the start of the word for 'his elders' is kept, and 'confined by' puts the man inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheen is a glossy shine or lustre, a synonym of brilliance.

clue.text: Birds don't start fighting around edges of the lake

indicators.note: don't start means the first letter is removed

parts.note: gulls are seabirds

indicators.note: around means the word for fighting goes round the other piece

parts.note: war is fighting

indicators.note: edges of picks the first and last letters of the word the

explanation.surface: Seabirds without a leader squabble on the shores of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Ullswater is a lake in England's Lake District, so 'the lake' is no generic reference; 'Birds' wants to be read whole but loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ullswater is one of the largest lakes in the English Lake District.

clue.text: Book on the bench?

definitions.meaning: to book is to make a booking in advance
a substitute player waiting on the bench in sport

explanation.definitionFit: To reserve is to book, and a reserve is a substitute player on the bench.

clue.text: Name of economist and army organiser

indicators.note: an organiser arranges things, so the letters are put in new order

explanation.surface: The economist's name and the officer who organises the army.
explanation.walkthrough: John Maynard Keynes was the economist; his middle name is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: John Maynard Keynes was the great British economist, so this is the economist's name.
